newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Key quotes from Yeltsin's state of nation address.
newsitem.headline: Key quotes from Yeltsin's state of nation address.

text.p: Here are some quotations from President Boris Yeltsin's annual state of the nation speech, delivered to Russia's parliament on Thursday and translated by Reuters.
ON ECONOMIC CRISIS
"Russia has entered 1997 with a heavy burden of problems. The situation in the country is extremely difficult and concerns the economy.
"The living standards of most of the Russian citizens, already low, are still sinking. People are suffering because of delays in payments of salaries, pensions and allowances.

"At the end of March people in many cities intend to take part in protest actions and these protests are to a large extent justified. This a warning signal, this is a sign that the patience of the people is reaching its limits."
"We are stuck half-way, having left the old shore; we keep floundering in a stream of problems which engulf us and prevent us from reaching a new shore."
ON THE GOVERNMENT'S RECORD
"Lack of will and indifference, irresponsibility and incompetence in resolving the problems of the state -- that is how people see Russia's authorities. I must admit this is correct.
"The authorities are getting fat...I am talking of those 'dignitaries' who are concerned only about their own well-being."
"Enough is enough. The country must be managed by authority and not by circumstances. We must restore order, first of all in the government, and I shall do this.
ON GOVERNMENT RESHUFFLE

"I have prepared a package of important and urgent measures. The structure and the composition of the government must be changed. New and competent people will come and I will announce these changes in the coming days."
ON NATO'S EXPANSION PLANS

"We are against NATO's plans for eastward expansion. Their realisation will deliver a direct blow to our security. Behind them is the aspiration to squeeze Russia out of Europe and to leave it politically isolated.
"NATO expansion can become a fateful decision which will cost the peoples of Europe very dear...We shall do everything possible not to allow a new division of Europe."
ON RUSSIA'S CONSTITUTION

"The Federal Assembly has passed only one third of the needed constitutional laws and there is already talk about changing the constitution. I am against such a hurry. First we have to learn to respect the constitution, live by it, use its full potential and only after that think about changes".

And in a warning to Russia's regional governors seeking greater freedom from the centre, he added: "It is impermissible to resolve regional problems by tearing apart the common political and economic space of the country...One may like or dislike Russia's laws but everyone must obey them."
ON CHECHNYA

"We have learned a lot from the crisis in Chechnya. Bloodshed has been stopped with huge difficulty. Talks continue. Confidence is being restored step by step but it is easy to destroy it and that is why it is dangerous to speed up the negotiating process artificially."
ON TAX REFORM
"Tax reform is this year's key economic task. We need to get to the point where arrears and non-payments stop being a major problem in the economy.
"Society is tired of waiting for tax reform. The existing system strangles enterprises. We will force everybody to pay taxes -- enterprises, famous politicians and businessmen."
ON THE FUTURE

"In 2000 Russia will elect a new president. I want to pass on to my successor a country with a dynamically growing economy, an effective and fair social protection system, a country whose people look to the future with confidence.
"I am offering cooperation to all political forces. I am sure that together we will be able to put things into order."
